easy.q: Elder Fale began and ended his talk with the same truth about himself and about each of us. What is it?
options: I am a child of God, and He loves me
I am strong enough on my own
I must earn God’s love each day
easy.why: Elder Fale said this statement is “powerful and empowering,” and that it is true “not just for me but for each of us and all of us.”

easy.q: What did Elder Fale and his wife show their children when they sat down together at home?
options: A picture of the family’s first home
A baby picture of each child
A picture of each child’s baptism
easy.why: After an impression at a Church meeting, Elder Fale asked his wife to find a baby picture of each of their children, and they looked at them together.

easy.q: Elder Fale told his children that the love he and their mother feel is a small part of someone else’s love for them. Whose?
options: Their grandparents’
Their teachers’
Their Heavenly Father’s
easy.why: He told them, “what we feel is but a small fraction of what your Heavenly Father feels for you.” Heavenly Father’s love is far greater than even a parent’s.

easy.q: In this talk, who did Elder Fale say is the evidence that God’s love is real?
options: Jesus Christ
The prophet Nephi
The Apostle John
easy.why: Elder Fale taught, “God’s love is real, and Jesus Christ is evidence of that love.” The Savior conquered sin and the grave to help His Father’s children.

easy.q: As a young boy riding home to his village, Elder Fale felt the Holy Spirit tell him something was true. What was he reading?
options: A copy of the Book of Mormon
A copy of the Church hymnbook
A copy of the New Testament
easy.why: He was reading a New Testament that gave John 3:16 in several languages, which begins, “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son.”

medium.q: Elder Fale asked his children what they had done, as babies, to earn their parents’ love. What point did he draw from their answer, “Nothing”?
options: Love they did not earn is love they cannot lose
Love grows as children learn to obey
Love has to be earned once we are older
Love is something babies cannot yet feel
medium.why: He told them there is nothing they can do to unearn that love: “You did not earn it; you cannot lose it. It is yours forever.”

medium.q: Elder Fale warned of a lie the adversary uses to twist the truth that God loves us. What is that lie?
options: That God loves only those who never sin
That God’s love was only for people long ago
That because God loves us, we can be saved regardless of our sins
That because God loves us, He will take away our trials
medium.why: Elder Fale said the adversary wants us to believe God’s love means we can be saved regardless of pride, rebellion, sins, or rejecting His Son and His Son’s servants.

medium.q: According to Elder Fale, what do we become immune to when we understand God’s love for us and for all His children?
options: The sorrows and trials of mortal life
The need to change and repent
The opinions of family and friends
The divisive, misleading labels of the world
medium.why: He said we become immune to the labels people put on us and on others, and instead “see ourselves and all of God’s children as beloved and divine.”

medium.q: Elder Fale mentioned the prodigal son and the shepherd leaving the 99 sheep to find the one. What did he use them to show?
options: That those who wander are loved more than those who stay
That there is still time if we turn to Christ today
That wandering from the fold carries no lasting cost
That we should wait for others to return on their own
medium.why: He said the Father’s message through His Son has always been “that there is still yet time if we turn to Christ today.” It is not too late to change.

medium.q: Elder Fale pointed out that the Savior taught us to pray to “our Father.” What did he say this shows?
options: That prayers should be offered together as a group
That prayers must always follow the same words
That the Father is only the Savior’s Father, not ours
That He is a loving Father to all of us, not just to the Savior
medium.why: Elder Fale said, “Not just His Father, not someone else’s father, but our Father,” a loving Heavenly Father who gives better gifts than any earthly father.

hard.q: Elder Fale said understanding our identity as God’s children is essential for happiness. What two other things did he say this understanding does?
options: Removes trials and promises an easier life
Prevents deception and gives purpose to mortal life
Ends temptation and makes repentance unneeded
Earns God’s love and sets us above others
hard.why: He testified that this truth “prevents deception and gives purpose to this mortal life.” Later in the talk he named the deceptions it protects us from.

hard.q: What did Elder Fale say to those for whom a loving family is not part of their earthly experience?
options: The divine pattern of families does not apply to them
They must wait until the next life to feel God’s love
Knowing Heavenly Father loves them can bring power, peace, and comfort
They can learn of God’s love only through studying the scriptures
hard.why: He said this knowledge brings “power, peace, and comfort” as we remember the eternal blessings, including an eternal family, that await all who make and keep sacred covenants.

hard.q: Elder Fale taught that God’s love for us is constant, yet he warned of a lie that twists this truth. How do the two fit together in his talk?
options: God’s love never ends, so covenants are helpful but not required of us
God’s love never ends, so all are exalted whatever they choose
God’s love ends when we sin and returns only after we fully repent
God’s love never ends, but exaltation requires receiving Christ and keeping covenants
hard.why: He said receiving Christ through priesthood ordinances and covenants, and being faithful to them, is “the only way to exaltation” and the only way to fully understand His love.

hard.q: In Elder Fale’s first reason, how does understanding the Father’s love lead us to become more like Jesus Christ?
options: We see why Christ works to save all, join that work, and grow like Him in it
We feel the Father’s love so fully that we grow like Christ without joining His work
We grow like Christ first, and that growth then makes us ready to join His work
We study what Christ did, copy it on our own, and so come to feel the Father’s love
hard.why: Understanding the Father’s love shows why Christ is anxiously engaged in saving all, which makes us eager to join Him. Then, “As we are anxiously engaged in this work, we are able to become more like Him.”

hard.q: Which person best shows the immunity to the world’s labels that Elder Fale described?
options: One who shrugs off labels put on her but still sorts others by theirs
One who trades the world’s unkind labels for kinder labels of her own
One who keeps away from people whose labels might harm her good name
One who sets aside labels on herself and on others and sees all as beloved
hard.why: He named “both the labels that people try to put on us and the labels the world tries to put on others.” Instead we see ourselves and all of God’s children as “beloved and divine.”
